t.E339.agn: In 2019 EFSA set a group acceptable daily intake (ADI) for phosphates of 40 mg/kg body weight, expressed as phosphorus. It reported that, together with phosphorus from all sources, average intake in infants, toddlers and children, and high intake in adolescents, may exceed this limit.
t.E339.body: Phosphate additives dissolve in the digestive tract and dissociate into free phosphate (orthophosphate); di-, tri- and polyphosphates are also converted to orthophosphate. About 80–90% of this phosphorus is absorbed; it is not converted into another substance in the body and is excreted in the urine via the kidneys.
t.E339.eff.0.t: Together with phosphorus from all sources, the daily limit may be exceeded
t.E339.eff.0.w: Infants, toddlers and children (average intake), adolescents (high intake)
t.E339.prod: Obtained chemically from phosphoric acid produced from phosphate rock.
t.E339.pw.0: According to EFSA, phosphate intake from all sources may exceed the daily limit in children.
t.E339.pw.1: According to EFSA, phosphate intake from all sources may exceed the daily limit in infants.
t.E339.regx.0: Re-evaluated; group ADI 40 mg/kg (as phosphorus); may be exceeded in children.
t.E339.summary: Salts of phosphoric acid. They regulate acidity, help raising and retain water in meat products; used in processed meat, processed cheese and baking powder.
t.E339.what: Regulates acidity; helps retain water and supports texture in processed meat and cheese. Phosphorus is a mineral the body needs and also occurs naturally in foods.
